subject: Private Offer: gross-to-net reconciliation & transaction-fee splitting
messages:
From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthsync.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer question — transaction fees / reseller margin

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up on two practical items we need clarified before we can move to internal approval:

1) Marketplace transaction fees (the AWS listing/transaction fee): does Redwood absorb that fee for private offers, or is it typically passed through to the customer / reseller? If passed through, how does that appear in gross-to-net and monthly reconciliation?

2) Channel margin math — our reseller network requires a 15% net margin on resold seat/usage revenue after any marketplace fees and taxes. We need a proposed way to show the math so our reseller can sign off on the deal.

We expect a committed starting run-rate of about $120k/month (first 12 months), with possible uplift in year 2. I attached our procurement spec (procurement_spec.pdf) and the draft reseller term sheet for context.

Can you put together the two reconciliation options and an example monthly invoice walk-through? That will let our procurement and reseller finance teams model the netback.

Best,
Claire
Claire Zhou
Head of Procurement
HealthSync

-- attachment: procurement_spec.pdf (PDF, 210KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer question — transaction fees / reseller margin

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear ask and for the spec. Looping in Laura from Deal Ops and Ben from Marketplace pricing so we can give a concrete example.

High level answers up front: we support both patterns depending on customer preference — (A) Redwood absorbs the marketplace transaction fee and adjusts list price / discount to preserve resale economics, or (B) the transaction fee is passed through and explicitly shown on the invoice; we then provide gross-to-net recon that credits the reseller appropriately. Each has tradeoffs for invoice clarity and unit economics.

Attached below are two quick scenarios and the assumptions we used. Can you confirm the reseller target margin (15% net) is on post-fee, post-tax net revenue? Also confirm whether the reseller expects to be invoiced by HealthSync (you) or wants direct invoicing routing to the reseller/vendor (this changes routing fields).

Option A — Redwood absorbs transaction fee
- Redwood takes the ~1.8% AWS transaction fee (example) out of our gross margin for the private offer.
- To preserve reseller netback, we typically increase the list price ~0.75–1.25% and then offer a slightly deeper private discount to keep customer effective price similar.
- Pros: reseller sees clean netback with no fee line item; easier for reseller to model.
- Cons: Redwood bears a small fee cost which we offset through minor list-price uplift or reduced rebate.

Option B — Pass-through on invoice
- We show the marketplace transaction fee as a separate line on HealthSync's invoice (or show as an invoice-level deduction).
- Gross-to-net reconciliations monthly show the fee and how it flows to reseller credit.
- Pros: transparent allocation of cost.
- Cons: requires reconciliations and can complicate reseller’s accounting.

Quick ask from us so we draft the example: confirm exact reseller entity name and whether the reseller will require monthly evidence (invoice + platform receipts) or quarterly netting. Also: is the 15% margin a floor or a strict target? If it’s a strict target we’ll propose a capped pass-through.

I can draft an invoice walkthrough for the $120k/mo scenario once you confirm those two items.

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthsync.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@healthsync.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer question — transaction fees / reseller margin

Hannah — thanks, this is helpful. Answers below:

- Reseller entity: Evergreen IT Resellers LLC (they need the evidence packet to show to their finance team).
- 15% is a hard target for the margin (reseller contract requires >=15% net margin after fees/taxes).
- Reconciliations: procurement wants monthly reconciliations (invoice + platform transaction receipt) and a capped pass-through if possible — they asked if Redwood would consider capping pass-through to 1.0% (instead of full 1.8%) for the first 12 months while Evergreen signs on.
- Invoice routing: HealthSync will receive the invoice and then resell; reseller does not want direct invoicing.

I attached our procurement term sheet and a short note from the reseller finance team (procurement_term_sheet.docx). Please draft an illustrative monthly walk-through for $120k committed, with both Option A and Option B math and a proposal for a capped pass-through.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement wants this to the reseller finance team by EOD tomorrow.

Claire

-- attachment: procurement_term_sheet.docx (DOCX, 85KB)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Claire Zhou <claire.zhou@healthsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer question — transaction fees / reseller margin

Claire — thanks for the details. Below is a concise mutual action plan and two worked examples for a $120,000 committed month. I attached a formal MOP (MOP-privoffer-v1.pdf) and our invoicing playbook (invoicing-playbook.md).

Mutual action items
- HealthSync: confirm reseller legal name for contract (Evergreen IT Resellers LLC) and provide reseller finance contact. Deadline: 2026-09-17.
- Redwood: produce monthly gross-to-net recon CSV and one-page evidence packet (invoice + marketplace receipt) within 7 business days of month close.
- Both: sign the one-year pass-through cap addendum if option B capped pass-through is accepted.

Illustrative math (assumptions)
- Committed gross invoice list price (before private discount): $120,000
- Estimated AWS transaction fee: 1.8% (= $2,160)
- Taxes (example sales tax): 0% (assumed out for this example; real taxes will be region-specific)

Option A — Redwood absorbs fee (recommended for simplicity)
- Redwood treats the $2,160 fee as an internal cost.
- To preserve Evergreen's 15% net margin, we set the private offer discount so the reseller netback = (list price - transaction fee - Redwood margin share) * reseller_split. Example calcs in attached MOP show the detailed steps; summary: Evergreen ends with ~15.1% net on the $120k scenario under our proposed list-price uplift + private discount.

Option B — Pass-through with capped fee (what procurement requested)
- Proposal: Redwood will cap pass-through to 1.0% for first 12 months (=$1,200) and carry the remaining 0.8% ($960).
- Invoice shows a transaction-fee credit line capped at 1.0% to the reseller netback calculation. Monthly recon will show full marketplace receipt and the capped credit.\n- Under this structure Evergreen’s net margin on the $120k example = ~15.0% after the capped credit (detailed steps in the MOP).

Recommended next step
- If HealthSync signs off on the capped 1.0% pass-through for year 1, we will:
  1) Add the pass-through cap addendum to the private-offer terms.
  2) Publish a 1-page evidence template Redwood will return each month (invoice + marketplace receipt + CSV netback).
  3) Run a sample reconciliation for August (dry run) and share with Evergreen finance.

Attachments referenced:
- MOP-privoffer-v1.pdf — worked examples, CSV template for recon, decision table on absorb vs pass-through.
- invoicing-playbook.md — invoice routing rules and sample invoice lines for private offers.

If that plan looks good I’ll route the pass-through cap addendum to HealthSync legal for signature. We can also do a 20-minute call with Evergreen finance if they want the walk-through.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

-- attachments: MOP-privoffer-v1.pdf (PDF, 320KB), invoicing-playbook.md (MD, 6KB)
